/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 23 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3000 (102)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4779 (277)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2149 (9)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1809 (-1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1074 (2)

CAPESIZE
The Capesize market got off to a positive start to the week, with gains driven primarily by a firmer Pacific, while activity in the Atlantic remained relatively subdued. The BCI 182 5TC increased by $2,519 to close at $43,346. In the Pacific, sentiment was firm, with two C5 miners active in the market. One miner led the way, paying a premium for an early 1 December arrival, eventually fixing at $15.90. Having covered this window, the bid subsequently eased to $15.25 basis 6 December, while a second miner was bidding $14.50 basis 7 December against offers in the upper $15s. This activity pushed C5 up by $1.278 to $15.678, while the C10 gained $6,165 to reach $47,277. The Atlantic, by contrast, had a sluggish start to the week across both basins. In the South Atlantic, bids for 13/23 December index dates were heard around $34,000, against offers closer to $36,000, leaving a considerable gap between owners and charterers. The C3 edged up by $0.218 to $34.936, despite the relatively muted activity. Overall, it was an encouraging start to the week, with the Pacific providing the momentum and driving the index higher, while the Atlantic awaits greater participation to establish a clearer direction.

PANAMAX
The week opened on a more positive footing, with both basins showing improvement, reflected in the P5TC increasing by $79 to $19,343. Brokers reported a tighter tonnage list, particularly off the North Continent for prompt dates, which coupled with increased demand has helped keep rates elevated. Market participants also noted a widening bid-offer spread as fundamentals continued to favour owners. With sentiment remaining positive and owners reluctant to concede, activity was said to be more limited today. Market sources reported an increase in demand from both Indonesia and Australia, with tonnage said to be tighter for prompt dates. As a result, some owners with slightly more forward positions were said to have withdrawn offers in anticipation of further upward momentum. The scrubber-fitted Atlantic Bonanza (82,143 2024) Zhanjiang 27/28 November was said to have been placed on subjects to Agricore for an Australia round trip in the low $20,000’s, while the Rio Hamburg (85,035 2022) Kuantan 25/26 November was also reported on subjects for a WC Australia round. Elsewhere, the Cemtex Innovation (81,326 2013) open Qingdao 25 November was said to be on subjects with Glencore for a coal stem from the North Pacific, while Oldendorff placed the scrubber-fitted AOM Sveva (81,625 2019) open Yokohama 29 November on subjects for a fertiliser stem from the North Pacific to China. The Sakizaya Diamond (81,938 2015) Hong Kong 25 November fixed a limestone stem from China to India with LDC, although no rate was reported. The Finder (75,618 2011) Zhoushan 17/19 November was also said to be on subjects for a China to India trip with fertiliser, with the rate again undisclosed. Period activity was also evident, with the Phaedra (82,053 2015) open Tachibana 01/06 December said to have fixed on an index-linked basis, although no further details emerged. Refined Success were meanwhile linked with the Ocean Pride (82,399 2021) Tianjin 29/30 November for a one-year period, although the rate was not reported.

SUPRAMAX
As usual a slow start to the new week, with very little change evident, meaning the 11TC average was down just $18 to settle at $22,866. All the rumours and reported trades were concluded last week, with the US Gulf remaining strong for November dates, whilst the rest of the Atlantic suffered from a lack of fresh enquiry. The slow eroding of rates in the Pacific appears to have be in a temporary lull in North Asia, but the weakness of the Indian Ocean is still a debilitating influence on South East Asia. The Norse Succession (66,280 2025) open Lake Charles was said to have fixed a petcoke stem to China with Bulk Trading at a time charter equivalent of $35,000 basis delivery SW Pass and the SSI Triumph (61,236 2014) Payra 28 November was reportedly fixed for a trip to China at $14,000, but no further details emerged. The CL Kiwami (66,295 2025) (scrubber fitted) open Jingtang 29 November-4 December fixed a trip to South East Asia at $25,000, whilst the Crimson Queen (58,140 2014) open CJK fixed a similar trip to Indonesia at $20,000, but in both cases the Charterer was not revealed.

HANDYSIZE
The week opened quietly, with limited activity reported across the market. The BHSI settled at 1,074, while the 7TC average increased by $33 to close at $19,329. In the Continent and Mediterranean, some fresh interest emerged, although rates generally held around last-done levels. The South Atlantic was similarly subdued, with little fresh information and charterers bidding close to previous levels, leaving the market broadly flat but resilient. The US Gulf maintained a firm, balanced tone, with rates holding steady at firm levels. Across Asia, fresh information was also scarce. Sources reported a continued increase in available tonnage, but rates remained largely steady. The African Teal (40,652 2015) open Singapore was placed on subjects for multiple legs at $18,500, while the V Pegasus (33,248 2008) open Dung Quat on 26–29 November was placed on subjects for a trip to Malaysia at $18,500. Further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore Imports by Source
Chinese iron ore imports fell 5.5 Mt year-on-year to a five-month low of 105.7 Mt in October, customs data show. Shipments declined from Australia (-1.7 Mt to 63.9 Mt), Brazil (-1.7 Mt to 24.1 Mt), India (-1.6 Mt to 0.3 Mt) and South Africa (-0.2 Mt to 3.9 Mt). Conversely, imports from Guinea rose from none to 2.7 Mt. However, in the year-to-October, total imports stood 32.4 Mt higher on the year at 1,060.6 Mt.

Chinese Bauxite Imports
Chinese bauxite imports rose 6.0 Mt year-on-year to 19.7 Mt in October, customs data show. Shipments from Guinea rose 6.3 Mt to 15.2 Mt, while imports from Australia ticked up 0.1 Mt to 3.9 Mt.
